A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R-Zero research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendix A are readable and support comparison despite substantive revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, pseudo-label accuracy analyses and supervised-data experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds iteration-scaling and parameter-sharing experiments in Figure 4 and Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The proposed Challenger–Solver GRPO loop, uncertainty and repetition rewards, format checks, majority-vote labels and difficulty filtering remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. Single-R-Zero is introduced as a parameter-sharing ablation of this retained method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven mathematical benchmarks, MMLU-Pro, SuperGPQA, BBEH, synthetic mathematical curricula and math12k supervised data. The new scaling and parameter-sharing analyses retain the mathematical task domain.

E2.justification: V3 adds the shared-parameter Single-R-Zero comparator in Table 6. Existing benchmark comparators remain: Table 2 relabels Base Challenger as R-Zero with a frozen challenger, while retaining the untrained base-model comparison.

E3.justification: The added analyses introduce 0.6B and 1.7B model settings, evaluation through four iterations, a shared-parameter control and a Gemini audit described as sampling 500 questions. The original 200-question GPT-4o audit remains. Table 2 changes Overall Avg. from averaging Math AVG and three general benchmarks to averaging only the three general benchmarks; existing decoding and Appendix A training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections 5.4–5.5 substantially extend the diagnostic evidence: Figure 4 examines when improvement reverses across model sizes, Table 5 examines pseudo-label accuracy around degradation, and Table 6 tests whether separating Challenger and Solver improves stability. V1's component ablations, difficulty analysis and supervised-data study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, independent repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The mean@32 decoding metric remains unchanged; the new audit sample count does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises four Qwen base-model scores, including Qwen3-4B GSM8K from 87.79 to 72.56. Table 2 removes iterations 1–2 and revises MMLU-Pro entries, including Qwen3-4B base/R-Zero from 37.38/51.53 to 50.58/55.47; Figure 1 updates the corresponding relative uplift from 37.9% to 9.7%. New results establish later-iteration degradation and weaker shared-parameter performance: Table 6 reports standard R-Zero falling from 49.07 at iteration 3 to 46.52 at iteration 4. The Gemini audit adds results under different conditions from the retained GPT-4o audit.

T1.justification: The GRPO formulation, reward definitions and Section 3.5 KL-divergence lower-bound argument are unchanged. The new stability discussion supplies empirical interpretations rather than new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of autonomous, zero-external-data co-evolution, reasoning improvements across backbones and domains, and synergy with labeled training. The headline +6.49 and +7.54 gains also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V1 already identifies declining pseudo-label accuracy as a potential bottleneck. V3 adds a broader limitation involving eventual performance degradation, interprets larger capacity as delaying it, and argues that label accuracy alone cannot explain instability. It proposes diversity loss, amplified biases and shared-model overconfidence as possible mechanisms.

D1.justification: Appendix A's hyperparameters, prompts and BLEU implementation details remain unchanged. V3 identifies Gemini for the new audit without specifying its version or prompt. It also omits the direct EasyR1 repository URL from the bibliography, while retaining the R-Zero code and math12k data links.

R1.justification: V3 adds connections to synthetic-data model-collapse literature, including Shumailov, Dohmatob, Seddik and Briesch, plus supporting citations on self-play, difficulty targeting and verification. It removes the Vision-R1 citation and associated multimodal-alignment example. The central positioning against seed-dependent and executor-dependent approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. V3 inserts Sections 5.4–5.5, makes localized wording corrections, adds a core-contributor designation and replaces the Technical Report running header with the paper title.

P2.justification: V3 redraws Figure 1's comparison panel with explicit task/solution crosses, a model legend and revised axis labeling. Table 2 is substantially compressed by removing the math column and intermediate-iteration rows. Figure 4 and Tables 5–6 are added, Table 3 moves, and headers and logos change.

improvement.justification: Sections 5.4–5.5 add valuable evidence about stability limits and the benefit of separate models. However, revised primary results introduce reporting inconsistencies: Table 1's Qwen3-4B base scores average 39.51 while AVG remains 42.58, and Table 2 implies a Qwen3-8B general-domain gain of 2.52 while Section 4.3 still states 3.81. Removing intermediate general-domain results also reduces transparency. These material diagnostic gains and reporting regressions prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
